prompt:
Original Taiwanese game art for "Tainan Gazetteer" (府城夜巡地圖), set in Tainan around 1930.
Style: handmade layered paper sculpture (紙雕 / kirie), the same for buildings, trees, plants,
fences, ground tiles, icons and props. Every shape is a piece of cut paper: visible paper fibres,
slightly soft hand-cut edges, pieces overlapping in shallow layers with small soft contact shadows
where one sheet sits on another. Colour is printed on the paper: clearly visible risograph /
stencil print grain and uneven ink density across every flat area, never a clean digital fill.
Weathering is welcome: irregular faded patches, not neat squares.
Details are built from few, large cut pieces (roof tiles, bricks, window frames, leaves, petals,
stones, planks), not painted lines and not crowded tiny patterns. Plants are natural and
asymmetric.
Colour: follow the real object, then mute it: pale, slightly greyed, warm. Typical tones: warm
cream, pale brick red, coral, sage and grey-green, mustard, indigo, wood brown, stone grey.
No saturated red-against-green contrast.
Buildings: strictly frontal elevation, no perspective, three or four flat paper layers.
Do NOT make: a 3D render or clay/plastic model, smooth bevelled relief, realistic or painterly
illustration, photo textures, thick foam layers, glow, glossy highlights, black outline strokes,
smooth gradients, depth of field.
Output: generated natively on a fully TRANSPARENT background (real alpha including enclosed
holes, no backdrop, no glow, no chroma-key colour, no coloured fringe), every object complete
and separated by clear transparent gutters, no ground, no base, no cast shadow outside the
object, no text, no captions, no logos.

Use case: stylized-concept
Single original game sprite: one mature flowering Taiwanese flame tree (Delonix regia), 130 game units tall, directly generated with artwork approximately 780 pixels tall and narrow transparent margins. Reference image 1 determines the broad rounded canopy and horizontally reaching angular branches only. Reference image 2 shows how to cut the iconic pinnate leaves only. Reference image 3: match the paper craft, bark folds and textured overlapping layers of the two trees in the bottom row only. Ignore the backdrops and glows in the reference images. Real specimen details from NParks: broad low umbrella, grey-brown spreading scaffold branches, fernlike leaves and coral-orange five-petalled flowers with one paler petal.
Exactly three distinct, plump, rounded masses of overlapping large sage and grey-green cut paper: large, medium and small, forming a scalene ikebana triangle with visible transparent gaps between them and bare supporting branches showing. Count nine prominent, 70–110 px long pinnate paper sprays total, only along irregular outer rims and undersides, projecting diagonally, each with a central axis and a few varied elongated leaflets on both sides. Cluster the flowers on upper and sunward rims: three well-separated bouquets of three overlapping flowers apiece, each with mixed flower sizes. Leave large quiet areas of plain rounded foliage and varying spacing. No small repeated round dots, stippled foliage motifs, extra flowers, buds or scattered petals. Crooked folded-paper warm grey-brown trunk, with clear angular changes of direction and taper, branching outward sideways, like the atlas cherry and maple. Flat cut paper layers, pronounced visible paper fibres and risograph grain, pale muted colors. Full tree including root flare in frame. Native alpha outside and in all gaps, no haze, glow or exterior shadows.
Composition for this candidate: large crown high near center, middle crown out and down to the right, small crown tipped down at far left. Short trunk and long staggered umbrella branches. Place the nine sprays unevenly, four on the large crown, three on the medium and two on the small. Keep each spray about one eighth of the tree height. Group each bouquet in an asymmetric arc with flowers partly overlapping. At generation scale fit the whole tree into the central area of the canvas with clear empty transparent padding on all four sides; if using a 1024 px tall canvas keep the visible tree about 780 px tall. Keep top petals and the outermost leaf tips comfortably inside the canvas. Keep alpha edges especially clean with no red, yellow or white residue.

notes: 使用內建 image_gen，以原生 alpha 分別生成四張，所有候選皆保留原檔。主圖選 candidate-4.png，有三團樹冠、三簇各三朵花、九片羽狀葉，四周有較多留白。生成畫布 1312 × 1199 px，alpha ≥ 128 的樹身約 1082 px 高，超出需求單約 780 px 的目標。依原則 10a 保留原生尺寸。邊緣有少量彩色半透明像素，待美術驗收。輸入圖依序為舊鳳凰木構圖、羽狀葉版本及核可紙雕圖集。實景參考 Singapore NParks 的整樹及花照片（https://www.nparks.gov.sg/publications-resources/articles/singapore-s-international-trees）與葉形、花形比較圖（https://www.nparks.gov.sg/florafaunaweb/resource/-/media/ffw/general/comparison-of-similar-plants/delonix-regia-and-peltophorum-pterocarpum---feb-2017.pdf）。
